messages:
riley: Heads-up — I pushed a small change to the SDK package exports and it broke the sample-runner when running on Node 18. Resolver picks the CJS path instead of ESM for dynamic imports. Repro in samples/starter

alex: ouch. can you paste the exports block from package.json?

riley: sure — here's the critical section:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  },
  "./lib/*": "./dist/lib/*.js"
}
```

riley: repro command I used: `node -e "import('..../packages/sdk').then(m=>console.log(m))"` — on Node 18 it throws `SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module` because it ended up loading the CJS file.

frankie: Node conditional exports order matters, but more subtle: resolver also considers the presence of a "types"/"main" field and subpath patterns. If someone publishes with both import/require and also has a legacy main, it can flip behavior.

mina: minimal repro here (paste):
```bash
# from repo root
cd samples/starter
node -v # 18.17.0
node -e "(async()=>{ await import('..../packages/sdk'); console.log('imported') })()"
```
error: `Error: Cannot find module '.../dist/esm/index.js'` (because pack tool published only cjs for that tag)

frankie: quick fixes: 1) ensure the package build includes both paths. 2) add an explicit fallback ordering — put `import` first (already is) but confirm published package.json preserves that order. 3) add a tiny integration test in samples that does a dynamic import on Node 18.

alex: could this be caused by our package publishing pipeline reordering keys? I remember a bundler that normalized package.json keys during pack.

riley: yep — publish step uses a script that merges manifests; it ended up stringifying then parsing which changed key order. Looks like Node's resolver is sensitive to how the conditional object is emitted.

frankie: fix plan: revert the canary release, push a patch that recreates the package.json with a deterministic writer (preserve conditional order), and add CI check that unpacks the tarball and asserts the exports block matches the expected string. I'll open a PR.

frankie: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/1234 — adds pack-time test + unit that validates export map and adds sample-runner dynamic import test.

ci-bot: build failed for samples/starter on node-18 (job 482): esm import test failed — see logs https://ci.internal/jobs/482

riley: nice, thanks for the quick turnaround. rolling back canary now and will coordinate a patched re-release. @frankie please ping when PR is green, we should also post a short note in #announce and update the onboarding doc so sample apps check for this. :+1:

mina: tiny follow-up: should we add a note in devex README about pack-time JSON key ordering? saved me a headache.

alex: agreed. Also consider a lint rule in the repo that serializes export maps with a stable writer.

riley: will do. thanks everyone.
